market_question: Russia x Ukraine ceasefire agreement by December 31, 2026?
reasoning: As of early 2025, the conflict shows no sign of a comprehensive ceasefire. Both sides hold maximalist positions (Russia demands territorial concessions and Ukrainian neutrality; Ukraine insists on full territorial integrity) that make a mutually agreed general suspension of hostilities unlikely within the next two years. While Trump administration pressure and war exhaustion could open a window, the gap between the parties remains wide, and past negotiations have failed. I estimate the true probability is around 42%, significantly below the market's 48.5% implied.
evidence_points: No previous agreement has met the resolution criteria after 3+ years of fighting
Both sides' publicly stated negotiation positions remain irreconcilable in early 2025
Western military aid to Ukraine continues, reducing the immediate pressure to concede; Russia still believes it can win on the battlefield
Historical ceasefire agreements in protracted similar conflicts typically take longer than 2-3 years to materialise without a decisive military outcome
sources_consulted: General news and analysis on Russia-Ukraine war status as of March 2025 (Reuters, BBC, ISW)
Polymarket description and resolution rules for this market
Historical precedents for ceasefires in interstate wars
